preamble: In celebration of an annual event that ends today

clue.text: Composer's been nursing tenor at seaside town

indicators.note: nursing means holding something within, so one word cradles the others inside it

parts.note: taken as written
T is the standard abbreviation for tenor in music
Hove is a seaside town in Sussex, beside Brighton

explanation.surface: A composer who has been looking after a tenor at a resort on the south coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Composer stands for 'is', a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludwig van Beethoven is among the most famous classical composers.

clue.text: Note: Brahms overture always turns up

indicators.note: an overture is the opening of a work, so it takes the first letter of Brahms
in a down entry, turning up reads the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: always means ever

explanation.surface: A musical observation that Brahms's overtures keep reappearing in programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is a musical note worth two semibreves, the longest in common use.

clue.text: Sort of band that's sensitive to changes in income

definitions.meaning: a stretchy rubber loop is one kind of band
in economics, demand is called this when it responds strongly to a shift in earnings

explanation.surface: A description of some kind of band whose fortunes rise and fall with its earnings.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a stretchy rubber band and income-responsive demand in economics take this adjective.

clue.text: Hearts lost injured scorer

parts.note: H is the card-playing abbreviation for hearts

indicators.note: injured suggests something knocked out of shape, so the letters of lost are rearranged

explanation.surface: A football report: Hearts lost a match after their goalscorer was hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts is a Scottish football club, which makes 'scorer' look like a goalscorer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorer here is someone who writes musical scores; Gustav Holst composed The Planets.

clue.text: 5–10 strings, excluding E strings

parts.note: read digit by digit as Roman V for five, I for one and O for zero

indicators.note: excluding says a letter is dropped from the word beside it

parts.note: strings means lines, as in fishing lines or cords
the letter E as printed

explanation.surface: An instruction about a range of five to ten string players, leaving out the E strings.
explanation.walkthrough: '5–10' looks like a range but is read as the characters 5, 1 and 0: V, I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Violins form the largest part of the orchestra's string section, often called simply the strings.

clue.text: Steal Handel's so-called familiar titles

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to steal
Handel's said aloud is 'handles', and handles are names; so-called flags the change of spelling

explanation.surface: A charge that someone pinched Handel's so-called pieces with familiar titles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handel's' is the composer only on the surface; heard aloud it is 'handles', slang for names.
explanation.definitionFit: Pet names are informal or familiar titles used in place of a real name.

clue.text: What cellists do on radio in The Boy Friend?

indicators.note: on radio means heard rather than read, so a word with the same sound is wanted

parts.note: cellists bow their strings

explanation.surface: A quiz question about what cellists in the pit do during a radio broadcast of The Boy Friend musical.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boy Friend is Sandy Wilson's 1950s stage musical; split up, its title also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is an old-fashioned word for a male suitor or sweetheart.

clue.text: The CBI managed to secure Ring for GM work, say

indicators.note: to secure means to hold something inside, so the shuffled letters close around the ring
managed suggests something handled and rearranged, so the letters of The CBI are reshuffled

parts.note: a ring is O-shaped, giving the letter O

explanation.surface: The business lobby group has arranged a Wagner Ring cycle to pay for genetic research.
explanation.walkthrough: The CBI is the Confederation of British Industry, a business lobby; Ring hints at Wagner's operas.
explanation.definitionFit: Genetic modification is an example of biotechnology, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Host a bishop and, according to Bach, a new church

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
German for 'and', the language of Bach
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone hosts a bishop and, following Bach, founds a new church.
explanation.definitionFit: A host can mean a great number, a multitude, as in a host of angels.

clue.text: Is Elgar distracted by love in rooms for wags?

indicators.note: distracted means thrown into confusion, so the letters of Is Elgar are jumbled

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A question whether the composer Elgar was distracted by romance in the WAGs' quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: WAGs is British tabloid slang for footballers' wives and girlfriends; here it covers wives in a harem.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the women's quarters of a Muslim palace, where wives and concubines lived.

clue.text: Refrain in Switzerland or America

parts.note: CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland
US stands for the United States

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a song's refrain is heard in Switzerland or in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorus is the repeated part of a song, the same thing as its refrain.

clue.text: Group in the other marquee forget note

parts.note: 'the other' is a coy British euphemism for sex

indicators.note: forget means leave out, so a letter is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: a marquee is a large tent
N for note is a standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A band forgets a note while playing in a different marquee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The other', as in 'a bit of the other', is British slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: A sextet is a group of six, especially six musicians.

clue.text: Subtle hint: tune in regularly during pub function

indicators.note: during puts the picked letters inside the pub and function words

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a do is a party or function

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of tune in is taken

explanation.surface: A sly suggestion to tune in regularly while at a party in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Innuendo is an indirect, usually suggestive, hint or insinuation.

clue.text: Pole's covering segment of Berenice capriccio

indicators.note: segment of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An extract from a lively Berenice piece described as covering a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: Berenice is a Handel opera, keeping the musical theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar regions are covered with a permanent sheet of ice.

clue.text: Roll up to study very old instrument

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study
a lute is a plucked string instrument

explanation.surface: Come along to study a very old instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: To convolute is to coil or twist something round on itself.

clue.text: Evidence I've translated about Köchel for composer

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jumbled letters surround a single one

parts.note: proof is evidence

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: K stands for Köchel, the cataloguer of Mozart's works, as in K. 525

explanation.surface: A musicologist's proof, rendered into another language, concerning Köchel's catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: This is an indirect anagram: 'translated' acts on the synonym of Evidence together with I've, and 'about' wraps the result around the Köchel letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei Prokofiev was a Russian composer, of Peter and the Wolf among much else.

clue.text: Variable speed acceptable in extremely showy work

indicators.note: in places the other pieces inside the outer pair
extremely takes the extreme ends of showy, its first and last letters

parts.note: Y is a variable in algebra
mph, miles per hour, measures speed
on means acceptable, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: A showy orchestral piece played at varying but acceptable tempo.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphony is a large orchestral composition, a classic example of a musical work.

clue.text: Beecham choir can randomly test sound here

indicators.note: randomly means in no set order, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Thomas Beecham's choir can be tested on sound quality at random.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Thomas Beecham was a famous English conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: An anechoic chamber absorbs all echoes, so acoustic engineers use it to measure sound and test equipment.

clue.text: See 16
Hundreds miss one cracking established work

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so the letters go inside the pair

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two make hundreds
a miss is a lass, a girl
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Hundreds fail to get one well-known piece right.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic is a work of recognised and lasting excellence.

clue.text: The way to tackle long instrument

indicators.note: to tackle means to take hold of, so the street abbreviation wraps around the yearning word

parts.note: St, short for street, is a way
to pine is to long for

explanation.surface: Advice on how to deal with a lengthy musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinet is a small harpsichord, a keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Boringly recites how basic scales progress

definitions.meaning: speaks in a dull monotone, as a priest chanting
read as two words: scales move up '...' and semitones

explanation.surface: Someone drones through an account of how simple scales go up.
explanation.definitionFit: To intone is to say something in a flat chanting voice; split up it is 'in tones', how a scale climbs.

clue.text: Drink firms suppress Consumers' Association note

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down, here keeping the association letters held between the two firms

parts.note: CO, short for company, twice for the plural firms
CA is the abbreviation for the Consumers' Association, a British watchdog
la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Drinks companies keep a consumer group's critical report quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: The best-known cola soft drink in the world goes by this brand name.

clue.text: Disconcert maestro

explanation.surface: A conductor is thrown off his stride.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle someone is to unnerve them; Sir Simon Rattle is a celebrated conductor.

clue.text: Barman left after party

indicators.note: after places the letter for left behind the party word

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: A bartender leaves once the party is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barman' is not a bartender: it is a man of musical bars, a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Ravel, composer of Boléro, worked in musical bars, making him a playful kind of barman.

clue.text: Subtle harmonies more than sufficient for composer

indicators.note: the two words contain more than enough letters to supply the name, which sits within them

explanation.surface: Delicate harmonies are more than enough for a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehár was the Hungarian composer of the operetta The Merry Widow.

clue.text: Note describes topless dance in big city

indicators.note: to describe can mean to trace a line around, so the note encloses the dance

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: topless means losing the top letter of the word beside it

parts.note: the rumba is a Latin American dance

explanation.surface: A newspaper item about a topless dance show in a large city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describes' means drawing a line round, so the note encloses the beheaded dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumbai, formerly Bombay, is India's largest metropolis.

clue.text: Intervals silence soprano, saving contest

indicators.note: saving here means keeping safe within, so the contest goes inside

parts.note: sh is an instruction to be quiet
an event is a contest in a competition

explanation.surface: Breaks in a concert hush the soprano while holding the competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A seventh is a musical interval spanning seven notes of the scale.

clue.text: Catch debut of Hammond organ

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so the first letter of Hammond is taken

parts.note: the ear is an organ of the body

explanation.surface: Catching the first performance on a Hammond organ.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hammond is an electric organ, but here organ means a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch what someone says is to hear it.

clue.text: He sings melodies using vowels, so clavier must be tuned

indicators.note: tuning adjusts an instrument, so the letters of so clavier are adjusted into a new order

explanation.surface: A singer of wordless tunes insists the keyboard must be tuned.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocaliser performs vocalises, melodies sung to vowel sounds without words.
